text: And thus is the application: the doubted validity is like invalidity, because it is an effect dependent on a cause other than the cause of knowledge. Validity is known externally; in the absence of practice, it is like invalidity due to the presence of doubt. Therefore, if it is claimed that validity is self-evident, even though it is external in both its origin and its being known (since it arises from a means of knowledge), such a claim is utterly absurd; indeed, it is like trying to punch the sky. While validity is produced by the components of cognition, the notion of its "self-evidence" arises merely from the wording, despite it being produced by a cause other than those components.
